# Independent root audit: affine reduction and high-sector closure


reduction in every d>=1, and for the stated triangle high sector
2/3<=a<=1. These are restricted results, not arbitrary OC.

The audited sources are
`candidate cebdfbe6dc0c0994`
and `candidate 77cefa95257c7b19`.
I also read the separate elementary d=2 affine-minimizer proof in full.

## All-dimensional radial mechanism

Radial disintegration from the fixed simplex vertex gives exactly
F_r(s)=d integral_0^r w^(d-1) T(s/w)dw, normalized by simplex volume.
The facet distribution is uniform, its projection has mean 1/d, and it
is atomless unless all continuous normal coefficients are equal. In
the nonconstant case the bracket of the deficit derivative has one
zero: the first tail is strictly between zero and one there, hence
strictly increases with radius until it reaches one. The other tail
is nondecreasing. The constant case is explicitly a positive-part
dth power difference and has its minimum at d(t-beta h)_+.

Ordinary facet Grünbaum gives T(1/d)>=Gamma_(d-1)>Gamma_d for every
nonconstant case, so the minimizing radius is strictly less than
d(t-beta h). In particular its smaller normalized threshold exceeds
t/R. This implies that along the line joining the original central
radius R to any later minimizing radius, BOTH normalized thresholds
increase. Evaluating the unique-root bracket further along that line
places the next minimizing radius above it. The proof also treats
the point where the line reaches zero and the case of a zero root;
there is no missing differentiability or support-knot assumption.

The original radius-drop secants increase, while minimizing-radius
secants strictly decrease. The stated separating interval is
nonempty by four explicit inequalities. Its affine line lies between
each original radius and its minimizer. This proves pointwise deficit
decrease. Nonnegativity of every replacement radius proves the
slope bound and makes the full radius interpolation concave. The
constructed body has actual integer fibers and contains the unchanged
central candidate. No volume preservation is needed: a negative
deficit remains negative under this comparison.

## Exact maximal-leg comparison

For an affine leg, beta>=lambda/3 lets each left triangle fiber alone
pay Gamma_2 times its area. In the remaining case both normalized
thresholds increase with h. Thus the normalized paired deficit
decreases. A negative sum on a finite prefix implies a negative last
positive-radius deficit; all appended positive-radius terms also
have negative deficit. Extending to the maximal affine leg preserves
violation. Zero-radius endpoints contribute nothing.

In the high sector both thresholds are in the upper tail or outside
support, so the two arithmetic sums in the source are exact. Their
affine summands are already negative at the real zero-radius index;
there are no fictitious nonzero terms beyond the source. The ranges
b in[1/3,1/2], 0<=z<=b, 0<k<=1 give nonnegative starting heights,
positive steps, and a strictly positive rational denominator.

The two elementary lower bounds for S(p,l) follow from its first
summand and convex trapezoids. The finite Faulhaber identity for the
upper bound on S(1,k) has the correct sign of its terminal cubic.
Its explicit bound gives the stronger remainder 3k/16<=k/5.

## Independent polynomial identity and positivity certificate

Let P=1-b, Q=P-kz. Independently clearing the scalar inequality's
denominator gives the compact polynomial

    N = 90(1-k)[P^3(1+z)+Q^3(1-z)]
        +135k(1+k)(1-z^2)[P^2+Q^2]
        -(40+60k+24k^2)(2-3b)(1-z^2).

Its denominator is 270k(2-3b)(1-z^2)>0. This independent derivation
uses the two separate lower bounds, not the author's expanded
polynomial. Substitute z=bv and map each of the two stated boxes to
the unit cube. `supporting computation verify_half_integer_affine_high_sector_root.py` uses
only standard-library rational sparse-polynomial operations. It
constructs all 250 Bernstein coefficients, verifies their exact
positive minima 5/2 and 331/384, and reconstructs each entire mapped
polynomial from the Bernstein basis. Both reverse identities pass.
The full coefficients are in
`supporting computation half-integer-high-sector-root-bernstein.json`.

The same checker independently verifies the finite arithmetic-sum
identity at 6975 rational cases; these checks are supplementary to
the uniform identity and inequalities, not a parameter-grid proof.

Consequently the relaxed scalar bound is strictly positive on the
whole required box. Each arithmetic sum dominates its stated convex
combination of lower bounds, while the target sum has the proved
upper bound. This completes the high-sector proof, including all
chain lengths and all real parameters.

The own central centroid belongs to the original source throughout.
The proof controls the specified original oblique halfspaces and the
opposite tilt by the established cross-label monotonicity. Its
continuous normal is nonzero, so every fiber boundary has area zero;
this does not dispose of other orientations, which are outside this
sector theorem. The factor is exactly Gamma_2/2=2/9. No restriction
on length survives and the older m<=11 reduction is unnecessary.
